В англійській порядок слів суворіший, ні: English word order is stricter than in Ukrainian. Adjectives line up in a set order (opinion, size, age, colour, origin, material), also, still, already and just have their own place next to the verb, enough goes after an adjective, and place comes before time.
Кілька прикметників перед іменником: дум: Several adjectives before a noun: opinion → size → age → colour → origin → material
She bought a beautiful long red dress.
also, still, already, just, always: пере: also, still, already, just, always: before the main verb, but after be
Макс завжди запізнюється, а ще забуває к: Max is always late, and he also forgets his keys.
yet: у кінці заперечення або питання: yet: at the end of a negative or a question
Ти вже закінчив есе?: Have you finished your essay yet?
enough: після прикметника, але перед іме: enough: after an adjective, but before a noun
Вода достатньо тепла? У нас достатньо ру: Is the water warm enough? We have enough towels.
We met at the station at nine.

після am / is / are / was / were: is sti: after am / is / are / was / were: is still, are also, was always
між допоміжним і основним дієсловом: hav: between the auxiliary and the main verb: have just done, has already left, will also come
yet у кінці заперечення або питання. sti: yet goes at the end of a negative or a question. In a negative, still goes before the auxiliary: I still haven’t ...
прикметник або прислівник + enough; enou: adjective or adverb + enough; enough + noun
дієслово + об’єкт + місце + час. Об’єкт: verb + object + place + time. Don’t separate the object from the verb.
Слово між дієсловом і об’єктом: A word between the verb and the object
Українською можна сказати «я дуже люблю: In Ukrainian you can put “very much” before or after the verb. In English the object comes straight after the verb, and very much goes after the object.
З прикметником enough стоїть після нього: With an adjective, enough goes after it: old enough, big enough. Don’t put it before the adjective.
Українською час часто йде першим, а англ: In Ukrainian time often comes first, but the normal English order is place first, then time.
Шпаргалка: черга прикметників: Cheat sheet: the order of adjectives
Рідко ставимо більше трьох прикметників: We rarely use more than three adjectives in a row. Adjectives from different groups don’t need commas between them. Table: group, example words, phrase.
Size before material: small leather. Adjectives have no plural, so smalls is wrong.
Розмір → колір → матеріал: small blue pl: Size → colour → material: small blue plastic.
Вік → колір → матеріал: old brown leathe: Age → colour → material: old brown leather.
just стоїть між has і основним дієсловом: just goes between has and the main verb: has just finished.
already перед основним дієсловом: alread: already goes before the main verb: already know.
Після be прислівник іде після дієслова:: With be, the adverb goes after the verb: is still. We don’t use yet in a positive sentence.
also перед основним дієсловом: also play: also goes before the main verb: also plays.
